title: Survival Croatian (draft A0, blocked on deck size)

days.title: One coffee, please
days.objective: You will order and drink coffee like a local, which in Croatia is a social institution rather than a transaction.
days.paretoFocus: Croatians go na kavu the way other countries go for a drink, and it can last two hours. Ordering is four words and buys you a seat at the most Croatian thing there is.
drills: Order your own real coffee out loud in Croatian before you drink it.
Say the size answer both ways without looking: veliku, malu.
Run the whole exchange from greeting to thanks.

items: How do you order one coffee?
What is being asked with veliku ili malu?
How do you say you want it to take away?

activities.title: At the counter
activities.intro: Whole phrases. The endings inside them are explained in A1; for now say them as they are.

items.note: Kavu is kava with an accusative ending, baked in. You will meet the rule in A1.
You will be asked this. Answer veliku or malu.

activities.title: Ordering
activities.intro: One phrase gets you what you want.

questions.prompt: You want your coffee to take away. You say:
questions.explanation: Za ponijeti is takeaway; za ovdje means you are staying.

questions.prompt: The barista asks 'Veliku ili malu?'. They want to know:
questions.explanation: Velika is large, mala is small, both in the accusative to match kavu.

questions.prompt: Going na kavu in Croatia usually means:
options: sitting and talking for a long time
questions.answer: sitting and talking for a long time
questions.explanation: The coffee is the excuse. Nobody will hurry you out.

questions.prompt: You want a second one. You say:
questions.explanation: Još jednu is one more, agreeing with kavu even when the word is left out.

activities.title: In the kavana
activities.intro: Coffee in Zagreb. Read both parts aloud, then only the Me lines.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.en: Good day! What would you like?

days.title: Paying
days.objective: You will pay by card or cash, ask for a receipt and understand the total.
days.paretoFocus: Croatia has used the euro since 2023 and cards are accepted almost everywhere, but markets, ferries and small konobas are still cash, which is exactly where you will be.
drills: Say both ways of paying out loud without looking.
Ask for the total and for a receipt, one after the other.
Practise the cash-only surprise: hear it, and answer in Croatian.

items: How do you ask to pay by card?
What currency does Croatia use?
How do you ask for the total?

activities.title: At the till
activities.intro: The four phrases that finish every transaction.

items.en: Could you give me a receipt?
I have no small change, sorry.

activities.title: Settling up
activities.intro: Pick what actually gets said.

questions.prompt: Croatia's currency since 2023 is:
questions.explanation: The kuna was replaced on 1 January 2023. Old prices are still quoted in it sometimes, in the same way as old money anywhere.

questions.prompt: You want to pay with your card. You ask:
questions.explanation: Karticom is the instrumental of kartica, the case used for by what means.

questions.prompt: Where should you still expect cash only?
questions.explanation: Carry some notes. The places worth going to are the ones least likely to take a card.

questions.prompt: 'Zadržite ostatak' tells the waiter:
questions.explanation: Tipping is modest here, and rounding up is normal rather than a percentage.

activities.title: The bill
activities.intro: Paying at the end of a meal. Read it twice.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Odmah. Bilo je sve u redu?
lines.en: Right away. Was everything all right?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.en: Yes, thank you. How much is it altogether?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.en: All right. I am paying cash.

days.title: Asking the way
days.objective: You will ask where something is and understand the four answers you will get back.
days.paretoFocus: Old towns here are stone mazes with no signage, and the answer is always one of four words. Understanding the reply matters more than asking well.
drills: Ask where three real places are, out loud.
Say the three directions from memory: left, right, straight.
Give somebody directions to your own door in Croatian.

items: How do you ask where the station is?
What does ravno mean?
How would a woman say she is lost?

activities.title: Finding things
activities.intro: Ask, then understand. The second half is what phrasebooks skip.

items.note: Swap the last word for anywhere: plaža, ljekarna, tržnica.
A woman says izgubila sam se.

items.hr: Možete li mi pokazati na karti?
items.en: Could you show me on the map?

activities.title: Following the answer
activities.intro: Match what you hear to what you do.

questions.prompt: Somebody says 'Samo ravno'. You:
questions.explanation: Ravno is straight ahead.

questions.prompt: You want to know whether to walk. You ask:
questions.explanation: The answer usually comes back as minutes rather than distance.

questions.prompt: A woman says she is lost:
questions.explanation: Past forms agree with the speaker, so a woman says izgubila.

questions.prompt: 'Pet minuta pješice' means:
questions.explanation: Pješice is on foot.

activities.title: To the station
activities.intro: Asking a passer-by. Read both parts, then only Me.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.en: Excuse me, where is the station?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.en: Go straight on, then turn right.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.en: It is not. Five minutes on foot.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Možete li mi pokazati na karti?
lines.en: Could you show me on the map?

days.title: Buses, trams and ferries
days.objective: You will buy a ticket, check you are on the right service and understand the departure time.
days.paretoFocus: The Croatian coast runs on ferries and the cities on trams, and neither waits. Three phrases keep you moving.
drills: Buy a ticket out loud to a place you actually want to visit.
Ask the departure time and the journey length, one after the other.
Say the difference between kolodvor and stanica without looking.

items: How do you ask for a return ticket?
What is a trajekt?
How do you check a tram goes where you want?

activities.title: Getting around
activities.intro: Buying and boarding, on land and water.

items.note: U jednom smjeru is one way.
Trajekt is the word you will need most on the coast.

items.hr: Ide li ovaj tramvaj do centra?
items.en: Does this tram go to the centre?
I am getting off at the next one.
How long does the journey take?

activities.title: At the window
activities.intro: One phrase per situation.

questions.prompt: You want to come back too. You ask for:
questions.explanation: Povratna is a return. U jednom smjeru is one way.

questions.prompt: Trajekt is:
questions.explanation: The islands are reached by trajekt, and in summer they fill up early.

questions.prompt: You are unsure the tram is right. You ask:
options: Ide li ovaj tramvaj do centra?
questions.answer: Ide li ovaj tramvaj do centra?
questions.explanation: Li turns a statement into a yes or no question, right after the verb.

questions.prompt: 'Izlazim na sljedećoj' tells people you:
options: are getting off at the next stop
are going to the last stop
questions.answer: are getting off at the next stop
questions.explanation: Useful on a full tram where the door is a long way off.

activities.title: Buying a ticket
activities.intro: At the ferry terminal. Read both parts, then only Me.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Dobar dan. Trebam kartu za Split.
lines.en: Good day. One ticket to Split, please.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: U šesnaest sati, s trećeg veza.
lines.en: At sixteen hundred, from berth three.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.en: How long does the journey take?

days.title: In the konoba
days.objective: You will get a table, order, say what you do not eat and finish well.
days.paretoFocus: A konoba is where the food actually is, and menus there are often only in Croatian. Five phrases open the whole meal.
drills: Order a whole meal out loud, from the door to the bill.
Say precisely one thing you never eat, in one Croatian sentence.
Ask for a recommendation and accept it, in Croatian.

items: What is a konoba?
How do you ask for a recommendation?
How do you say you do not eat meat?

activities.title: At the table
activities.intro: Door to bill, in eight phrases.

items.note: The single most useful question in a konoba. The answer is usually right.
A woman says ja sam vegetarijanka.

activities.title: Ordering well
activities.intro: The phrase that avoids the misunderstanding.

questions.prompt: A konoba is:
questions.explanation: Family run, usually small, and where the cooking is worth the trip.

questions.prompt: You eat fish but not meat. You say:
questions.explanation: Saying vegetarijanac would rule out the fish you actually want.

questions.prompt: Which question most reliably gets you the best dish?
questions.explanation: In a konoba the day's catch often is not on the printed menu at all.

questions.prompt: You want one bill for the table. You ask:
questions.explanation: Zajedno is together. Splitting is posebno, and small places would rather not.

activities.title: Dinner
activities.intro: An evening in a konoba. Read it twice.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Dobra večer. Stol za dvoje, molim.
lines.en: Good evening. A table for two, please.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.en: Here you are, here by the window.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.en: Here. Today we have fresh fish.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Lignje na žaru. Vrlo su dobre.
lines.en: Grilled squid. They are very good.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Ne jedem meso, pa to je savršeno.
lines.en: I do not eat meat, so that is perfect.

days.title: When you do not understand
days.objective: You will keep a conversation going when you have lost it, which decides whether you improve or give up.
days.paretoFocus: Croatians will switch to English the moment you hesitate. These six phrases are how you keep them speaking Croatian to you.
drills: Say all six repair phrases without looking.
Point at five things and ask how each is said in Croatian.
Use još učim in a real conversation today.

items: How do you ask somebody to slow down?
How do you ask what a word means?
Which sentence keeps people speaking Croatian to you?

activities.title: Buying time
activities.intro: Repair phrases. Worth more than the next hundred words of vocabulary.

items.hr: Kako se zove ovo na hrvatskom?
items.en: How do you say that in Croatian?

items.note: This one sentence usually makes people slow down instead of switching.

activities.title: When you get stuck
activities.intro: Pick the phrase that restarts the conversation.

questions.prompt: They spoke too fast. You say:
questions.explanation: It asks for pace, not for a translation, so the conversation stays in Croatian.

questions.prompt: You point at something you cannot name. You ask:
options: Kako se zove ovo na hrvatskom?
questions.answer: Kako se zove ovo na hrvatskom?
questions.explanation: It turns anything in front of you into a free vocabulary lesson.

questions.prompt: Which sentence most reliably keeps somebody speaking Croatian to you?
questions.explanation: It explains the pauses and invites patience rather than a switch to English.

questions.prompt: Why does asking to slow down beat asking for English?
options: you keep the practice and they keep the patience
it is considered rude to ask for English
questions.answer: you keep the practice and they keep the patience
questions.explanation: Most people here speak good English and will use it the moment you look stuck.

activities.title: Lost in the answer
activities.intro: Somebody answers faster than you can follow. Read it twice.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Autobus vam kreće s drugog perona, ali danas kasni.
lines.en: Your bus leaves from platform two, but today it is late.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.en: Sorry. I do not understand you.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.en: Platform two. The bus is late.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Razumijem malo. Napišite mi to, molim vas.
lines.en: I understand a little. Could you write that down?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.en: Thank you. I am still learning.

days.title: Getting help
days.objective: You will ask for help, find a pharmacy and say what is wrong.
days.paretoFocus: The phrases you hope never to need, which is why they have to be automatic rather than looked up on a phone you may not be holding.
drills: Say the emergency number out loud in Croatian.
Say all four help phrases without looking.
Find your nearest ljekarna and ask the way to it in Croatian.

items: What number do you call in an emergency?
What is a ljekarna?
How do you say you do not feel well?

activities.title: If something goes wrong
activities.intro: Say each one out loud now, so it is there later.

items.note: A woman says izgubila sam putovnicu.
112 reaches every emergency service across the European Union.

activities.title: In an emergency
activities.intro: One phrase per emergency.

questions.prompt: The emergency number in Croatia is:
questions.explanation: 112 works across the European Union and reaches all three services.

questions.prompt: You feel unwell in a shop. You say:
questions.explanation: It is the ordinary way to say it and will get you a chair and water.

questions.prompt: A ljekarna is:
questions.explanation: The pharmacist is the usual first stop for anything minor, as across Europe.

questions.prompt: A woman says she has lost her passport:
questions.explanation: The past form agrees with the speaker, so a woman says izgubila.

activities.title: At the pharmacy
activities.intro: You are unwell and go in. Read both parts, then only Me.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.en: Good day. I do not feel well.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.en: The surgery is across the road.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.en: Thank you. Where is the toilet?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.en: At the back, on the left.
